summary: Updates RFC 3777 to clarify whether sitting members of IETF leadership bodies, including the IAOC and ex officio members and liaisons, can volunteer for the nominating committee. It was replaced by RFC 7437.

eli5.summary: A rule says who may join a club's selection team. This clears up whether certain leaders and their helpers count as already on the team.

questions: who can volunteer for the ietf nomcom
are iaoc members eligible for the nominating committee
can iaab members volunteer for nomcom
subtitle: Clarify who cannot volunteer for the IETF nominating committee

tldr.problem: RFC 3777 said sitting members of the IAB and IESG cannot volunteer for NomCom, but it did not cover the IAOC, and was ambiguous about whether ex officio members and liaisons are included as sitting members.
tldr.mechanism: This update clarifies that any person serving on the Internet Society Board of Trustees, the IAB, the IESG, or the IAOC—including ex officio members—may not volunteer as voting members of the nominating committee, but liaisons are not excluded.
tldr.outcome: The eligibility rule is now clear and applies consistently to all leadership bodies, eliminating confusion about who can participate.

facts.label: Bodies covered
facts.value: IAB, IESG, IAOC, Internet Society Board of Trustees

today: RFC 6859 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 3777. It was later superseded by RFC 7437.

sections.title: The Eligibility Question
sections.content:
RFC 3777 defines the NomCom process, including a rule that sitting members of the IAB and IESG may not volunteer to serve as voting members of the nominating committee. The goal is to avoid self-selection: the bodies being filled should not pick their own successors.

However, when RFC 3777 was written, the IETF Administrative Oversight Committee (IAOC) did not exist. Also, the original text was unclear about whether ex officio members and liaisons count as sitting members.
sections.eli5: The old rule said certain leaders could not be on the selection committee, but it was unclear who exactly was a leader and if helpers counted.

sections.title: The Clarification
sections.content: Any person who serves on the Internet Society Board of Trustees, the IAB, the IESG, or the IAOC—including those who serve in ex officio positions—may not volunteer as voting members of the NomCom. Liaisons to these bodies from other organizations are not excluded by this rule, because they do not hold a seat on the body itself.
sections.eli5: Leaders of the IETF bodies cannot be on the selection committee. But people just helping out from other organizations can volunteer.

sections.title: Other Bodies
sections.content: The document notes that RFC 3777 does not exclude participation by working group chairs, research group chairs, members of directorates or review teams, or members of other advisory bodies. This restriction applies only to sitting members of the four leadership bodies named above.
sections.eli5: Everyone else—chairs of smaller groups and helpers on review teams—can still volunteer.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: This update to RFC 3777 clarifies the eligibility rule. It was itself later updated by RFC 7437.
sections.eli5: This cleared up the confusion, though the rules changed again later.
